### P-PASS FINDINGS

FINDING_ID: PF001  
ASSUMPTION: The stated objective is sufficient to validate the immune response layer by checking against the mathematical appendix, the 204 round-level findings from Experiment 15, and the 6 convergent findings.  
FALSIFIER: Important immune-layer failure modes exist that are not represented in the appendix or prior findings, so the experiment would only validate against historical issue sets rather than the actual behavior space.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
REVISION: Expand the objective to include prospective fault discovery via scenario-based testing of immune behaviors not previously reported, especially false-positive diagnosis, false-negative diagnosis, recovery thrash, damping misconfiguration, repeated model failure, and interaction with stop/allocation logic.

FINDING_ID: PF002  
ASSUMPTION: The in-scope code slice (~1,200 lines) is a coherent and sufficient representation of the immune subsystem.  
FALSIFIER: Critical immune behavior depends on code outside the extracted slice, causing reviewers to miss invariants, call-site assumptions, or state transitions.  
ASSESSMENT: UNCERTAIN  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
REVISION: Add a dependency manifest listing all external functions, classes, state fields, and config values referenced by the extracted subsystem; provide either their signatures/contracts or include read-only excerpts. At minimum include stop(), allocation interfaces, diagnosis consumers, and any state mutation helpers used by process_round/apply_diagnosis.

FINDING_ID: PF003  
ASSUMPTION: Out-of-scope exclusions are safe “unless immune response interacts with it.”  
FALSIFIER: Immune behavior materially depends on role assignment, load balancing, convergence detection, or diminishing returns, making interface-only review insufficient.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
REVISION: Replace the current out-of-scope wording with explicit interface obligations and test cases. Require targeted interaction checks for: immune-triggered reassignment, immune-triggered load changes, diagnosis effects on convergence/stop logic, and novelty-rate effects on immune actions.

FINDING_ID: PF004  
ASSUMPTION: Pre-applied fixes are correct and need not be revalidated in Experiment 17.  
FALSIFIER: One or more pre-applied fixes changed experiment behavior in ways that affect immune-layer observations or finding counts.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
REVISION: Add a preflight step that revalidates all Layer 1 engineering fixes with explicit acceptance checks: parser fixture corpus, watchdog kill test, timeout propagation test, and experiment-numbering test. Treat these as environment invariants before live execution.

FINDING_ID: PF005  
ASSUMPTION: The 6 convergent findings are the right context set for Round 0.  
FALSIFIER: Providing them anchors models, suppresses independent discovery, and biases blind-round evidence.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
REVISION: Split Round 0 into two phases: 0A fully blind with no prior findings, 0B informed validation with the 6 convergent findings. Compare overlap and incremental yield. Use 0A for independence evidence and 0B for resolution validation.

FINDING_ID: PF006  
ASSUMPTION: “Standard CDSFL adaptive rounds” is operationally specific enough for execution.  
FALSIFIER: Reviewers or operators cannot reproduce allocation, novelty handling, challenge flow, or stop escalation consistently from the plan alone.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
REVISION: Add an execution protocol appendix defining per-round inputs, required outputs, novelty adjudication, challenge/defense handling, model failure recovery behavior, and stop/defer authority.

FINDING_ID: PF007  
ASSUMPTION: DynamicManager can safely control adaptive rounds while itself being part of the test article.  
FALSIFIER: The system under test influences the orchestration of the test, masking faults or altering evidence generation.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
REVISION: Decouple control from evaluation. Use either a fixed external controller for Experiment 17 or shadow-run DynamicManager decisions against an external overseer that logs divergences and prevents self-judging stop/allocation decisions from being authoritative.

FINDING_ID: PF008  
ASSUMPTION: Stop condition validity can be trusted because fix 4.1 was applied and 350 tests pass.  
FALSIFIER: The stop predicate remains wrong in live adaptive conditions despite unit coverage, especially under noisy or sparse novelty trajectories.  
ASSESSMENT: UNCERTAIN  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
REVISION: Add explicit scenario tests and live telemetry for stop() inputs/outputs across rounds, including a post-hoc stop audit showing why the experiment stopped and whether an earlier/later stop would have changed findings materially.

FINDING_ID: PF009  
ASSUMPTION: Verification via code review, unit testability, mathematical consistency, and cross-model agreement is sufficient to validate findings.  
FALSIFIER: A finding can satisfy those checks yet still be operationally wrong because runtime behavior under adversarial round sequences was not exercised.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
REVISION: Add behavior-driven simulation as a required verification path for immune-layer findings: inject synthetic failures, attrition, oscillation, and recovery scenarios and verify diagnosis/action trajectories over multiple rounds.

FINDING_ID: PF010  
ASSUMPTION: Cross-model agreement by 2+ models is a reliable verification signal.  
FALSIFIER: Models share the same anchored context or same misunderstanding, producing correlated agreement.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
REVISION: Downgrade cross-model agreement from verification criterion to corroborative evidence. Require one independent artifact in addition: test, trace, code path proof, or counterexample.

FINDING_ID: PF011  
ASSUMPTION: SymPy verification is mostly not applicable.  
FALSIFIER: Immune-layer decisions embed threshold or state-transition logic that can still be formalized or exhaustively checked without SymPy being irrelevant.  
ASSESSMENT: HOLDS  
SEVERITY: 0.22  
REVISION: No major change needed, but add “property-based or state-machine checking” as the formal fallback for logic-heavy claims where symbolic math is not the right tool.

FINDING_ID: PF012  
ASSUMPTION: Applying fixes in descending severity order is safe.  
FALSIFIER: A high-severity fix depends on a lower-severity prerequisite or interacting fix, causing churn, invalidation, or misleading regressions.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
REVISION: Change fix ordering rule to “dependency-aware severity order.” Build a small fix DAG first; apply prerequisites before dependents, then sort remaining independent fixes by severity.

FINDING_ID: PF013  
ASSUMPTION: Running the existing test suite after each fix is an adequate regression gate.  
FALSIFIER: The existing suite lacks coverage for immune-layer regressions, so harmful changes pass the gate.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
REVISION: Add subsystem-specific regression tests before applying immune-layer fixes. Minimum required suites: diagnosis classification, recovery action propagation, damping behavior, repeated-failure handling, stop/continue transitions, and interaction with reassignment/load signals.

FINDING_ID: PF014  
ASSUMPTION: Reverting on regression and flagging for human review is sufficient failure handling.  
FALSIFIER: Multiple interacting fixes each regress alone but succeed together, so immediate revert loses valid remediation paths.  
ASSESSMENT: HOLDS  
SEVERITY: 0.41  
REVISION: Keep revert-on-regression as default, but add a branch for “suspected interacting fixes”: quarantine into a staging branch with dependency notes rather than discarding outright.

FINDING_ID: PF015  
ASSUMPTION: “All 6 convergent findings resolved” is a meaningful success criterion for Experiment 17.  
FALSIFIER: The experiment resolves those 6 while missing more serious immune-layer faults.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
REVISION: Reframe this as a minimum condition, not a success criterion. Add primary success criteria based on defect detection quality, protocol robustness, and validated runtime behavior under induced scenarios.

FINDING_ID: PF016  
ASSUMPTION: “At least 3 models survive to round 3+” is an appropriate success criterion.  
FALSIFIER: Survival count is driven by infrastructure quirks or conservative stopping, not immune-layer quality.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
REVISION: Replace with measured resilience metrics: attrition rate by cause, successful recovery rate, median rounds survived after first failure event, and whether immune actions improved continuation relative to a baseline or shadow controller.

FINDING_ID: PF017  
ASSUMPTION: “Ascending abstraction guard demonstrably fires during the experiment” is a valid success criterion.  
FALSIFIER: The experiment is healthy and never enters a state requiring that guard, so non-firing is not failure.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
REVISION: Replace with “guard behavior is validated.” Require either natural firing or injected scenario tests that demonstrate both fire and non-fire cases with expected decisions.

FINDING_ID: PF018  
ASSUMPTION: “Findings curve shows genuine decay” can be reliably measured by novelty rate from DiminishingReturnsDetector while that area is otherwise out of scope.  
FALSIFIER: The detector itself is imperfect or its output is influenced by immune actions, making the measure circular or unstable.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
REVISION: Add an independent novelty audit by the collator on a sample of findings, and define a secondary decay metric not solely dependent on DiminishingReturnsDetector.

FINDING_ID: PF019  
ASSUMPTION: The listed risk mitigations cover the major execution risks.  
FALSIFIER: Important unlisted risks remain, such as control/test contamination, anchoring bias, insufficient coverage, API nondeterminism, logging gaps, and inability to reproduce round decisions.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
REVISION: Extend the risk register with at least: self-orchestration bias, blind-round anchoring, missing telemetry, nondeterministic API behavior, partial-context extraction error, and novelty adjudication inconsistency.

FINDING_ID: PF020  
ASSUMPTION: DeepSeek’s existing “halved max_tokens retry” is adequate mitigation for empty response risk.  
FALSIFIER: Empty or low-quality responses are caused by context load, prompt structure, or decomposition mismatch rather than token budget alone.  
ASSESSMENT: UNCERTAIN  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
REVISION: Add a response-quality fallback ladder: retry once, then reduced-context decomposition, then structured checklist prompt, then mark degraded participation with separate analysis weighting.

FINDING_ID: PF021  
ASSUMPTION: The plan provides enough telemetry to support post-mortem review.  
FALSIFIER: After execution, operators cannot reconstruct why diagnoses were made, why actions were taken, or why models were retained/culled.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
REVISION: Mandate round-level logging of diagnoses, triggering signals, damping state, recovery actions, allocation decisions, stop inputs, stop outputs, and per-model failure classifications.

FINDING_ID: PF022  
ASSUMPTION: The plan’s verification and execution steps are reproducible across runs.  
FALSIFIER: API nondeterminism, mutable prompts, or changing code slices prevent meaningful comparison across runs or later audits.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
REVISION: Freeze the code snapshot, prompts, model versions, config values, and extracted line ranges by hash/commit ID; store full experiment manifest with artifacts.

FINDING_ID: PF023  
ASSUMPTION: A single experiment pass is enough to validate immune behavior.  
FALSIFIER: Observed behavior is highly path-dependent, and one run does not cover realistic failure sequences.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.81  
REVISION: Add at least one replay or scenario-based batch: baseline run, induced-failure run, and stress run. Compare immune outcomes across them.

FINDING_ID: PF024  
ASSUMPTION: Severity scoring can be applied without a defined rubric.  
FALSIFIER: Reviewers assign inconsistent severity, distorting fix ordering and triage.  
ASSESSMENT: FAILS  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
REVISION: Add a severity rubric combining consequence, likelihood, detectability, and scope of impact, with anchor examples for 0.2/0.5/0.8/0.95.

### OPEN QUESTION RESPONSES

Q1: DeepSeek should get per-area decomposition, and the other models should at least receive a dependency manifest plus optional segmented views.  
Justification: ~1,200 lines is borderline manageable for strong models but risky for weaker long-context performance, especially when the task is not summarization but adversarial review. DeepSeek already has a decomposed role mode, and the immune layer contains multiple distinct subareas: diagnosis structures, health monitoring, failure handling, round integration, and diagnosis-to-action mapping. Decompose for DeepSeek into those areas plus one integration pass. Keep full-context access available for final synthesis. This reduces omission risk without depriving stronger models of system context.

Q2: Do not provide the 6 convergent findings in the truly blind phase; provide them only after independent discovery.  
Justification: If you include them in Round 0, it is not blind in any meaningful sense. It becomes a validation/anchoring round. The better design is two-phase: Round 0A independent discovery with no prior findings, then Round 0B validation against the 6 convergent findings. That gives you both independence evidence and resolution checking. This directly reduces correlated agreement bias.

Q3: Set immune_damping_rounds to 1 for the 5-model pool during live execution, with a predeclared fallback to 2 only if oscillation is observed in replay or pilot traces.  
Justification: In a 5-model pool, damping of 2 rounds is relatively sticky and may delay legitimate recovery/adaptation, especially when you want to observe immune responsiveness rather than suppress it. Since this experiment is validating the immune layer itself, over-damping risks hiding defects and reducing experimental sensitivity. A value of 1 preserves some anti-thrash protection while allowing faster feedback. If pilot traces show oscillatory overreaction, promote to 2. Without those traces, 2 looks conservative but under-informative. Recommendation: default 1, document fallback threshold for switching.

Q4: Test load balancing separately, but include explicit interaction checks in this experiment.  
Justification: Pulling the full load-balancing layer into scope will expand the state space and dilute the immune review. But excluding it entirely is unsafe because immune actions may trigger or be triggered by balancing decisions. The right split is: keep full load balancing out of scope, include the interface contract in scope, and add interaction scenarios covering rebalancing triggers, capacity pressure, and allocation side effects. That preserves tractability while covering the real coupling risk.

### PROPOSED IMPROVEMENTS

IMP001: Add an external or shadow controller for experiment orchestration.  
Justification: The current plan lets DynamicManager both be tested and control the test. That is the largest validity risk in the plan.

IMP002: Split Round 0 into Round 0A blind and Round 0B informed validation.  
Justification: This preserves independence evidence and avoids anchoring while still checking the known convergent findings.

IMP003: Add scenario-based runtime simulations as a first-class verification method.  
Justification: Immune behavior is dynamic. Static code review plus unit tests is insufficient for stateful recovery logic.

IMP004: Require an interaction matrix across immune layer, role assignment, load balancing, convergence detection, and diminishing returns.  
Justification: Current scope boundaries are too soft and risk missing coupled faults.

IMP005: Define a full telemetry schema before execution.  
Justification: Without round-level traces, post-mortem analysis of immune decisions will be weak or impossible.

IMP006: Freeze the experiment manifest by commit hash, prompt versions, model versions, and config snapshot.  
Justification: Reproducibility is currently under-specified. [VERIFY:current]

IMP007: Add induced-failure test cases before live execution.  
Justification: Validate behavior under synthetic empty responses, repeated failures, false health alarms, delayed recoveries, and oscillating model quality.

IMP008: Replace success criteria based on incidental events with behavior-validation criteria.  
Justification: “guard fires” and “3 models survive” are weak proxies. Use recovery correctness, false-positive/false-negative rates, and controlled continuation quality instead.

IMP009: Add an independent novelty adjudication sample reviewed by CC1/human.  
Justification: Reliance on DiminishingReturnsDetector alone is circular when novelty measurement is part of the evaluated system boundary.

IMP010: Create a dependency-aware fix application DAG.  
Justification: Severity-only ordering is brittle when fixes interact.

IMP011: Add subsystem-specific regression tests before applying any new immune fixes.  
Justification: Existing tests alone are not a credible gate for this layer.

IMP012: Define explicit model-failure categories and handling rules.  
Justification: Empty response, malformed output, timeout, contradiction, and low-substance output should not all collapse into one recovery path.

IMP013: Add a degraded-mode protocol for weak or partial participants.  
Justification: The plan currently assumes all models remain comparably useful. In practice, degraded but nonzero participation should be preserved and weighted, not treated as binary alive/dead.

IMP014: Add a severity rubric.  
Justification: Triage without a common rubric will be noisy and may distort ordering.

IMP015: Add a “no-fix-needed” evidentiary standard.  
Justification: Two convergent findings are already marked no-fix-needed. The plan should specify what evidence is required to uphold that judgment during Experiment 17.

IMP016: Add a post-experiment audit section.  
Justification: Require a final report comparing planned vs actual rounds, immune interventions, attrition causes, and whether stop/allocation decisions appear justified.

IMP017: Narrow language around “validated.”  
Justification: The experiment can increase confidence, not prove correctness. Replace “validate” with “evaluate and stress-test” where absolute validation is implied.

IMP018: Include one adversarial isolated pass if operationally feasible.  
Justification: A fresh-context pass aligns with CDSFL’s modular/adversarial logic and is useful here because prior-round context is likely to bias later reviewers.

IMP019: Add explicit acceptance thresholds for open-question outcomes.  
Justification: For example, if decomposition is used, specify how findings from decomposed and full-context passes will be merged and deduplicated.

IMP020: Add a rollback and quarantine protocol for interacting fixes.  
Justification: Immediate revert is good for safety, but promising interacting fixes should be staged rather than lost.

Definitive stance: the plan is not execution-ready as written. The main blockers are self-orchestration by the system under test, blind-round anchoring, insufficient dynamic verification, and missing telemetry/reproducibility controls. Fix those before running Experiment 17.
